title: Tokenize multicast subscriptions to prevent premature StrictMode listener teardown

violation.problem: multicastSubscribe stores subscriber callbacks in a Set<(data: T) => void>. When a React component with a stable callback reference double-mounts in StrictMode, the Set only contains 1 entry. The first cleanup deletes the callback, reducing subscriber count to 0 and triggering grace-period detachment while mount 2 is active.
violation.expectedSolution: Assign a unique subscriber ID or subscription handle to each multicastSubscribe call, tracking subscribers by handle so cleanup for one handle does not delete active sibling handles.

steps: In studio/src/lib/subscription-pool.ts, change subscribers from Set<(data: T) => void> to Map<number, (data: T) => void> or a ref-counted subscriber collection.
In multicastSubscribe(), generate a unique numeric or string handle ID for the subscription and store subscribers.set(handleId, callback).
In the returned unsubscribe function, delete by handleId (subscribers.delete(handleId)).
reviewChecklist: StrictMode double-mounting with stable callbacks does not detach listener
Listener is cleanly detached after all active handles unsubscribe
Cached snapshots are still delivered immediately to new handles
